audit_findings.title: Projected growth may be treated as costless
audit_findings.magnitude: computed first-year implied growth investment: $179.1 million in base and $223.9 million in bull; full valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth increases OE without an explicit deduction for the incremental capital and working capital required; using 26.3% RONTA, first-year reinvestment equals OE growth divided by RONTA.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate that future growth of our business will require increased manufacturing capacity from our third-party supply foundries, assembly shops, and testing facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated model omission unless growth reinvestment is already embedded elsewhere in forecast OE. The disclosed method grows the $588.8 million maintenance-style anchor by 8% or 10% while merely reporting, rather than applying, RONTA. The implied first-year deductions equal 30% and 38% of anchor OE, respectively, and recur as the business grows, so they are reasonably capable of materially lowering operating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to net income, D&A, total capex, supplier deposits and working-capital changes; then rerun every forecast year with explicit growth reinvestment based on incremental OE and the filed 26.3% RONTA, avoiding any double counting.

audit_findings.title: Finite tax incentive may be capitalized as a perpetual benefit
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 tax burden embedded in anchor OE flows through the forecast and terminal cash flow without an explicit tax-rate normalization when the ten-year incentive expires.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2024, one of the Company’s foreign subsidiaries was granted a ten-year tax incentive, beginning in tax year 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The incentive begins in 2025 and has a ten-year life, placing its expiration at approximately the model's transition to perpetuity. The model contains no stated post-expiration adjustment, while terminal value represents 52.6% of base operating PV and 53.7% of bull operating PV. The post-incentive cash tax rate is not established, so the overstatement cannot be quantified, but the affected component is large enough to be material. The separate $1.1 billion deferred-tax benefit is an accounting amount and cannot itself be treated as the valuation impact.
audit_findings.action: Establish the incentive's exact expiration and utilization schedule, forecast cash taxes after expiration including applicable Pillar Two effects, confirm the 2024 deferred-tax benefit was excluded from OE, and rerun the terminal value using normalized post-incentive taxes.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may not be worth face value to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $968.7 million of foreign-held cash and short-term investments exposed; actual haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds $1,413.761 million of cash and short-term investments at face value even though $659.5 million of cash and $309.2 million of short-term investments were held by foreign subsidiaries and some foreign earnings are indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.evidence: An actual repatriation of the undistributed earnings could be subject to additional foreign withholding taxes and U.S. state taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed numbers place 68.5% of the bridge cash and short-term investments abroad. Repatriations of $140 million in first-half 2026, $275 million in 2025 and $642 million in 2024 had minimal or immaterial tax impact, which limits evidence for a broad haircut, but the filing also says other foreign earnings remain indefinitely reinvested and could incur withholding and state taxes. The record does not identify which balances are distributable or the minimum operating cash requirement, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 cash and investment balance by legal entity and jurisdiction, identify restricted or operationally required balances, calculate jurisdiction-specific repatriation taxes, and rerun the bridge using only net distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Quarter-end cash may be paired with an undeducted dividend payable
audit_findings.magnitude: $101.683 million, equal to approximately $2.00 per diluted share and 0.83% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds June 30 cash while omitting the June 30 dividends and dividend-equivalent liability included in other accrued liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, accrued dividends totaled $76.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 10-Q demonstrates that $101.683 million of dividends and dividend equivalents was accrued at quarter-end, including $98.3 million of declared dividends. If gross quarter-end cash is used, this liability must be deducted. The correction lowers value by about $2.00 per diluted share, versus base value of $242.54 and a market price of $1,221.235, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the filed $101.683 million from the cash bridge, or document that the liability was paid and the cash balance was correspondingly reduced before using a later cash date; rerun per-share values and the buy-below price mechanically.

audit_findings.title: Tax-related source data remain exposed to a control weakness
audit_findings.magnitude: known prior restatement was $194.642 million; any current valuation error is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Erroneous tax data could alter historical OE, the $588.8 million anchor, cash-tax assumptions or tax-related bridge liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we identified a material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting.
audit_findings.explanation: The control weakness is demonstrated and remained unremediated at June 30, 2026. It previously caused a $194.642 million reduction to 2024 net income and retained earnings, although that correction concerned deferred taxes and therefore need not equal an OE error. The June 2026 comparative statements do incorporate the disclosed restatement, but the record does not establish whether every valuation input was sourced from the corrected filings or whether another misstatement exists. Direction and valuation materiality therefore remain uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Trace every 2024 and 2025 tax, net-income and cash-flow input to the restated 2025 10-K; confirm the June 2026 balance-sheet and comparative inputs agree to the restated figures; separately prove that noncash deferred-tax benefits were excluded from OE; rerun only if discrepancies are found.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved litigation remains a contingent claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse judgment, settlement, uninsured defense cost or related regulatory action would reduce bridge cash or future OE, but no litigation liability is deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: The Securities Action and Derivative Litigation seek unspecified amounts of damages and/or attorneys’ fees and other relief.
audit_findings.explanation: The proceedings existed at June 30, 2026, expanded to include another derivative suit, and seek unspecified damages, fees and other relief. Management did not consider a material loss probable, so no demonstrated omitted accrual is established. However, first-half 2026 SG&A included a filed $10.1 million year-over-year increase in legal expense, showing a current cash-flow channel even though the contingent loss itself cannot be sized. Without claimed damages, an estimable range or insurance information, materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-filing docket developments, claimed damages or settlement demands, counsel's loss range, D&O insurance limits and exclusions, and defense-cost coverage; normalize recurring legal expense in OE and deduct any subsequently probable and estimable uninsured liability from the bridge.
